notes: Guards three things about work that predates the call. (1) Turn 1 names an existing job (the Pellegrino sweep) and a new day but never says which day it is on now (it is four days out): Claire must find the row by name and move it, not add a new one. (2) Turn 2 is an immediate reversal ('undo that, put it back where it was'): the same row must go back to today+4, so the final state is the original placement, exactly one Pellegrino row, none on tomorrow (tomorrow and today+4 never coincide). The row is listed in seededRowsMayChange because it legitimately moved twice; count 1 plus maxRowsAdded 0 fail a Claire that re-creates it instead of moving it, and the absent check fails one that leaves the first move in place. (3) Turn 3 names the Ostrander rain cap and gives the instruction in the same breath ('take it off'): the row must be gone from every date (the absent check carries no date), without a confirming question. Nothing new is authorized, so maxRowsAdded is 0. Every line is a named instruction or a question, so zero authorization asks; a 'should I move it back?' or 'want me to take it off?' is the friction this guards. Turn 4 is a question and must get a real answer naming the surviving Thackeray inspection (mustMention), which must match the database. The rods pickup on today is never mentioned and must be untouched.
